front: Black tailed deer from behind: what do you see?
back: Wide tail, dark brown or black on top for most of its length; small white rump patch (90%).

front: Mule deer tail vs black tail?
back: Mule deer: thin white tail, black tip only. Black tail: wide, dark on top almost all the way (90%).

front: Black tailed deer ears vs mule deer?
back: About 3 cm shorter (90%, Nyberg and Janz 1990).

front: What does a raised black tail show?
back: A broad white underside (80%, WDFW).

front: Black tailed buck weight in BC?
back: About 48 to 90 kg (90%, BC deer account).

front: Black tailed doe weight in BC?
back: About 40 to 65 kg (90%).

front: Chest height of an adult coast black tail?
back: About 57 cm (90%, Vancouver Island data).

front: Where do the biggest south coast bucks come from?
back: The fertile lower Fraser Valley, and migratory deer that feed high in summer (90%, Nyberg and Janz).

front: What share of yearling black tailed bucks are spikes?
back: About 90% (90%). About 10% have one more point a side.

front: By what age do most black tailed bucks have forks?
back: About 2.5 years: 2 points a side (90%).

front: Is a spike legal in MUs 2-8, 2-18, 2-19?
back: Yes. A buck bears visible bony antlers (page 4), and those rows say Bucks (page 28) (99%).

front: Antlerless deer season in 2-8, 2-18, 2-19?
back: None. Bucks only (99%, page 28).

front: White tailed deer season in Region 2?
back: None (99%, pages 14 and 27).

front: Which licence does a black tailed buck use?
back: The deer species licence that covers mule deer: "mule (black-tailed) deer" (99%, pages 8 and 27).

front: Days of hunting per deer in MU 2-18, 2020 to 2024?
back: About 25 (24.6, computed, 90%). Region 2 average about 13.5.

front: Where are coast black tails in spring and summer?
back: Often in logged openings for new green food (90%, BC deer account).

front: What is key coast winter range?
back: Old growth, and steep south to west facing slopes (90%).

front: Snow depth that is hard going for deer?
back: Deeper than about 30 cm (90%, BC deer account).

front: Same snowfall: clearcut vs 70% conifer cover?
back: About 50 cm in the clearcut, about 5 cm under the trees (90%, Nyberg and Janz).

front: How far apart are a migrant's summer and winter ranges?
back: Often 2 to 5 km (90%).

front: Share of deer that migrate: moderate vs deep snow zone?
back: About 20 to 25% vs 70% or more (90%).

front: Winter range order near Harrison?
back: UWR (Ungulate Winter Range) U-2-006, Chilliwack district, for mule deer and black tailed deer (95%).

front: Capable winter range in U-2-006: which slope directions?
back: 135 to 285 degrees: south east through south to west; slopes 40 to 100% (95%).

front: Snow zones in U-2-006?
back: Shallow under 400 m, moderate 400 to 800 m, deep over 800 m (95%).

front: Coast winter foods?
back: Douglas fir, western redcedar, red huckleberry, salal, deer fern, tree lichens (90%).

front: When are deer most active?
back: Near dawn and dusk; they can move any time (80%, WDFW).

front: Legal hunting hours for deer?
back: 1 hour before sunrise to 1 hour after sunset (99%, page 11, item 38).

front: Good security cover hides how much of a deer at 60 m?
back: About 90% (85%). Look for parts, not a whole deer.

front: Strongest deer sense?
back: Smell (85%). Keep the wind in your face.

front: When do Vancouver Island black tails breed?
back: November and early December; most does conceive 15 November to 5 December (90%).

front: How long is a doe receptive?
back: About a day. Not bred? She cycles again in 22 to 29 days (90%).

front: How long does a buck tend a doe?
back: Follows 2 to 3 days before her heat, stays 3 to 4 days after (90%).

front: When are black tailed bucks heaviest?
back: About mid November to early December; they lose 20 to 25% over winter (90%).

front: Where do coast deer use a clearcut most?
back: Within about 100 m of cover (90%, Nyberg and Janz).

front: Clearcut width that gets the most deer use?
back: Under 200 m wide, so under 100 m to cover from anywhere (90%).

front: Can you push deer with a truck?
back: No. Using a motor vehicle to herd or harass wildlife is unlawful (99%, page 11, item 25).

front: Rain and a blood trail?
back: Rain can erase blood within about an hour: only sure shots, track sooner (Tip).

front: Broadside aim point?
back: Up the back of the front leg, one third up the chest (85%).

front: Kill. What comes first?
back: Cancel your licence, then touch the deer (99%, page 11).

front: Evidence of sex for a buck?
back: The unskinned tail AND a testicle or part of the penis, naturally attached (99%, page 15).

front: Region 2 compulsory inspection for deer?
back: No. Region 2 inspection is for mountain goat and cougar (99%, page 28).

front: Meat cooling target?
back: Below 4°C (40°F) as fast as you can (80%, WDFW).

front: Plastic on warm meat?
back: No plastic bags or tarps until it is chilled. A tarp as a roof with an air gap is fine (80%).

front: Ageing temperature and time?
back: 1 to 3°C (34 to 37°F), no longer than two weeks (80%, WDFW).
